topic_summary: Analysis of the personhood boundary in abortion law: the contested determination of when moral and legal status begins, which structures the victim set, rights allocation, and state authority to regulate abortion. This is a foundational kernel where different readings of the personhood commitment generate structurally incompatible constraints.

key_entities: Religious institutions (interpretive authorities for natural law readings)
key_tensions: Fetal moral status vs maternal autonomy (zero-sum in rights allocation)
State police power vs individual liberty (scope of legitimate regulation)
Fixed textual commitment vs evolving social consensus (constitutional interpretation method)
key_mechanisms: Gestational limits (state enforcement of personhood boundary through criminal/civil penalties)
Judicial review (courts adjudicate boundary disputes via constitutional interpretation)
key_absences: Economic coercion structures (how poverty shapes 'choice' independent of legal access)
Medical gatekeeping power (physician discretion as de facto boundary enforcement)
Interstate legal arbitrage (how federal structure enables boundary shopping)

omegas.description: Economic coercion substrate deferred: poverty structures access independent of legal boundaries. Travel costs, childcare, lost wages create de facto personhood boundaries that differ from statutory ones. Mountain or Piton?
omegas.source: Deferred axis economic_coercion_substrate + Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan)

omegas.description: Cross-national personhood boundaries not examined: European gradualist frameworks, Islamic jurisprudence ensoulment traditions, East Asian regulatory models. Do these reveal structural alternatives or confirm the kernel's universality?

Viability threshold drifts with NICU technology; conception detection drifts with pregnancy testing. Does technological change reclassify the kernel readings or merely shift their empirical boundaries?

Four readings identified (conception, viability, birth, gradualist). Are there structurally distinct readings from non-Western or non-Abrahamic traditions that would pass the individually-holdable test?

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Four disciplinary lenses applied (constitutional law, bioethics, political philosophy, federalism). Dark matter probes surfaced economic substrate and international comparison gaps, documented as omegas. Kernel structure recognized and decomposed into four readings plus three independent axes.

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The personhood boundary: when moral and legal status begins, determining victim set composition and rights allocation
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Contested across traditions — religious natural law, constitutional originalism, philosophical autonomy frameworks, medical professional standards

readings.commitment: Moral and legal status begins at conception (fertilization)
readings.authority_grounding: Natural law / religious doctrine (Catholic, evangelical Protestant traditions)
readings.expected_structural_delta: Fetus enters victim set at conception; abortion becomes homicide-equivalent; state authority maximized; maternal autonomy subordinated to fetal rights

readings.commitment: Moral and legal status begins at viability (capacity for independent survival)
readings.expected_structural_delta: Fetus enters victim set at ~24 weeks; state interest becomes compelling at viability; pre-viability abortion protected; post-viability regulable

readings.commitment: Moral and legal status begins at birth (complete expulsion from mother)
readings.expected_structural_delta: Fetus never enters victim set; pregnant person sole rights-holder throughout pregnancy; state authority minimized to health regulation only

readings.commitment: Moral status develops gradually; legal status follows developmental milestones
readings.expected_structural_delta: Victim set composition changes across trimesters; state interest increases with development; balancing framework rather than bright-line rule

axiom_contradictions.basis: Conception reading's axiom (moral status at fertilization makes abortion homicide-equivalent) is mutually exclusive with birth reading's axiom (only born persons hold rights; bodily integrity is absolute pre-birth). No single coherent framework can hold both: accepting one requires rejecting the other's foundational claim about when rights-bearing begins.

Conception reading grounds status in biological event independent of technological capacity; viability reading grounds status in technological threshold. These are incompatible foundations: one treats personhood as natural-law fact, the other as contingent on medical capability.
